nodes.label: sequentially consistent
nodes.def: The strongest memory ordering requiring a single total order of all sequentially consistent operations visible to all threads; implied by default for std::atomic operations in C++.

nodes.label: memory order relaxed
nodes.def: C11/C++11 memory ordering that only guarantees atomicity of the operation with no ordering constraints relative to other operations; allows all reorderings.

nodes.label: c11 memory model

nodes.label: exponential backoff
nodes.def: Contention management strategy backing off exponentially after failed lock acquisition; reduces bus traffic and collision; common in spinlock and CAS-based algorithm implementation

nodes.label: thundering herd contention surge
nodes.def: A transient spike in the rate of lock or resource acquisition attempts triggered by mass wakeup, producing queue buildup and wasted retry cycles.

nodes.label: acquire semantics
nodes.def: Memory ordering semantics ensuring all subsequent loads/stores cannot be reordered before the acquire operation; used for lock acquisition, reading a flag after volatile write.

nodes.label: mcs lock

nodes.label: jitter
nodes.def: Randomized variance introduced into the computed delay to decorrelate competing threads and mitigate thundering-herd synchronization on lock release.

nodes.label: release semantics
nodes.def: Memory ordering semantics ensuring all prior loads/stores cannot be reordered after the release operation; used for lock release, writing data before a volatile flag.

nodes.label: seq cst global total order

nodes.label: atomic cas
nodes.def: Compare-and-swap operation atomically loading a value, comparing it to an expected value, and storing a new value only if they matched, returning whether the swap occurred.

nodes.label: bounded buffer
nodes.def: Classic synchronization problem with fixed-size buffer between producers and consumers; requires empty/full conditions and mutual exclusion; solution uses semaphores or monitors.

nodes.label: current delay
nodes.def: The computed wait interval for the current retry iteration; derived from base_delay multiplied by backoff_multiplier raised to the iteration count, then capped by delay_ceiling.

nodes.label: deadlock
nodes.def: Liveness failure where two or more threads wait indefinitely for conditions held by each other; occurs with circular wait, hold-and-wait, no preemption, and mutual exclusion.

nodes.label: spinlock

nodes.label: atomic operation

nodes.def: Protocol resolving priority inversion by temporarily elevating the priority of a lock-holding low-priority thread to match the highest blocked thread.

nodes.label: producer consumer
nodes.def: Concurrent pattern with producer threads generating work consumed by consumer threads; typically synchronized with bounded or unbounded channels/queues.

nodes.label: race condition
nodes.def: Behavior where program outcome depends on relative timing of interleaved operations on shared state; general term for any timing-dependent bug in concurrent programs.

nodes.label: rcu read copy update
nodes.def: Linux kernel synchronization mechanism allowing read-heavy workloads without reader locks; readers access data freely while writers make copies and schedule updates for later recla

nodes.label: recursive mutex
nodes.def: Mutex variant permitting the same thread to acquire the lock multiple times; must be released same number of times; can hide design problems but necessary in some recursive pattern

nodes.label: relaxed vs seq cst

nodes.label: seq cst atomic visibility

nodes.label: seq cst atomic visibility no intermediate state visibility
nodes.def: During the execution of a seq_cst load or store, no intermediate memory state is visible to any thread; the operation is indivisible and appears instantaneous to all observers in t

nodes.label: seq cst default atomic ordering
nodes.def: The default memory ordering for std::atomic operations in C11/C++11 when no memory_order is explicitly specified; provides the strongest guarantees without requiring explicit fence

nodes.label: seq cst fence
nodes.def: The explicit memory fence with sequentially consistent ordering that provides both acquire and release semantics plus additional ordering constraints to enforce the global total or

nodes.label: seq cst program order preservation
nodes.def: Within each thread, sequentially consistent operations maintain program order; no reordering of these operations is permitted within the same thread.

nodes.label: serializability
nodes.def: Correctness criterion for transaction systems requiring equivalent to some serial execution of transactions; differs from linearizability in handling multiple operations per transa

nodes.label: speculative execution
nodes.def: CPU technique executing instructions before their need is confirmed (e.g., branch prediction); rolled back on misprediction; interacts with memory ordering when speculative loads s

nodes.label: starvation
nodes.def: Condition where a thread is perpetually denied resources needed for progress due to scheduling or contention patterns; unfair lock implementations may starve waiters.

nodes.label: store buffer
nodes.def: Hardware structure buffering stores before they become visible to other cores; essential for TSO performance but creates visibility delays requiring memory barriers to manage.

nodes.label: test and set
nodes.def: Atomic operation setting a memory location to a value (typically 1) and returning its previous contents; basis for simple spinlock implementations.

nodes.label: thread local storage
nodes.def: Per-thread data storage allocating distinct instances to each thread; avoids synchronization for thread-private data; accessed efficiently without locking.

nodes.label: thundering herd fairness starvation
nodes.def: A degraded thread fairness condition where some members of the wait_set are repeatedly overtaken by newly arriving competitors, never acquiring the resource despite eligibility.

nodes.label: thundering herd jitter decorrelation
nodes.def: Application of jitter to retry delays using full_jitter, equal_jitter, or decorrelated_jitter to prevent synchronized re-attempts among awakened threads, breaking retry_coordinatio

nodes.label: thundering herd phased awakening
nodes.def: A staged wakeup strategy dividing waiters into cohorts awakened in sequence rather than simultaneously, damping the contention surge through temporal distribution.

nodes.label: thundering herd wake one semantics
nodes.def: A notification strategy where at most one waiter is awakened per signal, eliminating the surge by design; the canonical mitigation for thundering-herd in mutex and condition-variab

nodes.label: ticket lock
nodes.def: Fair lock implementation using atomic ticket counter where threads take a ticket number and spin-wait until their number is called; ensures FIFO ordering and prevents starvation.

nodes.label: volatile java
nodes.def: Java modifier ensuring visibility of writes across threads; provides acquire/release semantics on reads and writes; different from C++ volatile which lacks memory ordering guarante

nodes.label: wait free
nodes.def: Strongest progress guarantee requiring every thread to complete any operation in finite steps regardless of other thread interference; no starvation possible.

nodes.label: work stealing
nodes.def: Load balancing strategy where idle threads steal work from busy threads' queues; typical in fork-join frameworks like Java ForkJoinPool; reduces contention compared to work distrib

nodes.label: store buffer linger
nodes.def: A relaxed store may remain in a store buffer indefinitely before becoming visible to other threads; no fence or ordering constraint forces a flush.

nodes.label: volatile cpp
nodes.def: C++ qualifier historically used for optimization barriers; in modern C++ standard, only provides address volatility semantics, not memory ordering; use std::atomic instead.

nodes.label: wake all semantics
nodes.def: Blocking primitive behavior — e.g., pthread_cond_broadcast, SetEvent, or equivalent — that resumes all waiting threads rather than selecting one; the direct cause of the wake spike

nodes.label: wake latency spread
nodes.def: Metric: the distribution of acquisition latencies among threads woken simultaneously; wide spread indicates thundering herd while tight clustering indicates controlled awakening.

nodes.label: wake one semantics
nodes.def: Blocking primitive behavior that resumes exactly one selected waiter per wake event; the canonical counter-pattern to wake_all_semantics.

nodes.label: wake ratio
nodes.def: Metric: threads woken per successful acquisition; a thundering herd has wake_ratio >> 1, ideally 1.

nodes.label: wake spike
nodes.def: The acute moment of mass simultaneous thread wake-up from a blocking primitive; the event horizon of the thundering herd.

nodes.label: waste ratio
nodes.def: Metric: fraction of awakened threads that re-block without acquiring; directly measures the cost of a thundering herd episode.

nodes.label: work bag pattern
nodes.def: A mitigation where the producer deposits work items into a lock-free queue and only one consumer wakes; avoids notifying all waiters entirely.
